description:
Worldsmith Console Commands
Reshape the Persean Sector from the console.
v1.2.0 for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

Ever wanted to drag a gas giant out to the edge of a neutron star system, hide a moon in its shadow where the pulsar beam can't reach it, found a brand-new faction with its own flag and lore, and then plunge the whole sector into total war? Worldsmith does all of that with plain-word console commands, no file editing needed.

Download: latest release (GitHub)
Requires: Console Commands, LazyLib, Nexerelin
Can be added to a running save, but not removed from one.
Java: runs on Java 27 (tested with Mikohime) and on the game's standard Java 17.
Most of the code was written by AI (Claude Opus 5.5).

What you can do

Build worlds: planets, moons, rings, asteroid and debris fields, companion stars, or whole new star systems, black holes and neutron stars included.
Bend orbits: push a planet farther out or speed it up, in percent, reverse it, or tidally lock a moon behind its planet.
Terraform and tweak: change a planet's type, size or color, and rename planets, systems and whole factions.
Found factions: a new Nexerelin faction with its own name, flag, lore, ships and personality.
Steer the 4X: set each faction's share of colony expeditions in percent, strengthen or weaken factions, send armadas, start rebellions.
End it all: total war, total peace, or the apocalypse: Remnant raids, orbital bombardment or revolution.

New in 1.2.0

orbit: distance and speed in percent, reverse, and tidallock for moons.
expeditions: set any faction's share of Nexerelin's colony expeditions in percent, or how often they come.
resizeplanet works in percent now.

All commands
Here are all commands and their options. You can also read them in the README on GitHub, or in the game: open the console with Ctrl+Backspace and type help worldsmith or wshelp.
Type names as shown on the map: case doesn't matter, underscores count as spaces, and IDs work too. Without a name, most commands use the planet whose dialog is open. Options in [brackets] are optional, and a|b means "a or b".

Spoiler
Looking things up
showsystem [system]: every planet, moon and station of a system, with type, hazard, owner and resources.
planetinfo [planet]: everything about one planet: size, orbit, industries, its conditions and how much each adds to the hazard.
planettypes [filter] / startypes [filter]: all planet or star types, modded ones included. The filter shows only types whose name contains it.
visit <planet|station|star>: opens its dialog from anywhere.
findplanet <filters>: searches the sector and lists the nearest 20 matches. Combine any of:
a condition such as farmland_rich, or a group such as farmland, ore or ruins (wshelp conditions lists them all)
-toxic_atmosphere: must not have it
habitable, uncolonized, colonized
type:jungle: that planet type
hazard<150: hazard below 150% (also <=, >, >=)
within:20: at most 20 light-years from you
owner:hegemony: colonies of that faction
all: also planets you haven't surveyed

Example: findplanet habitable farmland hazard<150 within:20

Planets and colonies
terraform [planet] <type> [keep]: changes an uncolonized planet's type and rolls new conditions that fit it (planettypes lists the types).
keep: only the type changes and the conditions stay; this also works on colonies

rename <current name> <new name>: renames a planet, station or colony.
put a > between the names if you're unsure where the current one ends
with a planet's dialog open, just rename <new name>
rename system <system> <new name>: the system, its star and the planets named after it (Glith I becomes Hakeball I). Stars always follow their system's name.
rename faction <faction> <new name>: a faction, everywhere; reset as the new name undoes it

recolor [planet] <color>: tints a planet, moon or star. Only the look changes.
red, orange, yellow, gold, green, teal, cyan, blue, purple, pink, white, grey, brown, black
a hex color such as #3080ff
random
reset: the standard look of its type

addplanet [type|random] [name]: a planet at your distance from the star, generated like vanilla's.
addmoon <planet> [type|random] [name]: a moon at your distance from the planet, or in its first free orbit.
moveplanet <planet>: moves it, with its moons, to your distance and angle.
resizeplanet [planet] <percent|auto>: makes it wider or narrower.
a percentage: 150% makes it 1.5 times as wide, 200% twice as wide, 50% half as wide
auto: a normal size for its type

orbit [planet] [options]: changes the orbit of a planet, moon or companion star. Without options it shows which way it circles and how many days one orbit takes. Options can be combined:
distance 150%: 1.5 times as far out (50% = half as far). It keeps its speed, so a wider orbit takes longer.
speed 200%: twice as fast (50% = half as fast)
reverse: circles the other way
tidallock: for moons. The moon always stays behind its planet, away from the star, in the planet's shadow, where a neutron star's pulsar beam can't reach it. speed or reverse ends the lock.

Moons, stations and rings move with it. Example: orbit Corvus_V distance 150%, then orbit Corvus_VA tidallock.
popcap [colony] <size|off>: the colony stops growing at that size. It never shrinks a colony.
off: removes the cap

treatasnpccolony [colony] [off]: Nexerelin treats it like its own expedition colonies: the AI builds it up as it grows, and Nexerelin's size limit for such colonies applies.
off: removes that mark

Systems, stars and space
newsystem <name> [star type] [full|empty]: in hyperspace, a new star system at your position, with an inner and a fringe jump point. A popup asks how to fill it, unless you say so in advance:
full: planets, moons, rings and stable locations, like a random system
empty: only the star

Without a star type it picks one at random; black holes and neutron stars work too. The star is called "<name> Prime".
addstar [star type|random] [name]: a second or third star at your position, orbiting the main star: a binary or trinary system.
addring [planet] <type>: around the star at your distance from it, or around the named planet.
belt: an asteroid belt with asteroids
dust: a dusty ring that looks like debris
ice: an ice ring
magfield: a magnetic field

addobject <type>: at your position, orbiting the star.
stable_location: an empty stable orbit, where a relay, buoy or array can be built
comm_relay: helps the stability of colonies in the system
nav_buoy: fleets travel faster in the system
sensor_array: better sensor range in the system
comm_relay_makeshift, nav_buoy_makeshift, sensor_array_makeshift: weaker versions
inactive_gate: a gate

Relays, buoys and arrays start unclaimed, so you claim them like any other.
addfield <asteroids|debris> [small|large]: at your position.
asteroids: an asteroid field
debris: a debris field you can salvage
small / large: its size (otherwise in between)

addjumppoint [name]: a two-way jump point where you are. In a system, it leads out to hyperspace; in hyperspace, it leads into the nearest system (at most 3 light-years away).
hyperclouds <clear|add> [radius]: in hyperspace, around you.
clear: removes the clouds and the storms in them
add: grows new clouds (star systems keep their clear space)
radius: 0.5 to 5 light-years, 1 if you leave it out

Removing things
Everything here asks Yes/Cancel first.
removeplanet <planet> / removemoon <moon>: uninhabited planets and moons, and the second or third star of a system. Rings and debris around them go with them.
removering [planet] [belt|ring|magfield]: without a planet, the belt, ring or field around the star nearest to you. With a planet, all its rings, or only the kind you name.
removeobject [type|name]: the nearest object where you are, the nearest of a type, or one by name.
stable, relay, buoy, sensor, gate: the objects addobject makes
field: an asteroid or debris field
jumppoint: a jump point made with addjumppoint (both ends)

New factions
spawnfaction <name> [options]: founds a new faction. A popup asks for anything you leave out and shows the planets before anything happens.
here / random: in your system, or at a random empty place ("Pick another place" rolls again)
small / medium / large: 1, 3 or 5 colonies
red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple, pink: its color on the map. There are 8 slots, one per color; spawnfaction list shows which are free.
like <faction>: it uses that faction's ships, weapons and way of fighting. Without it, a random faction's.

It gets a random player flag and empty lore, and Nexerelin runs it like any other faction: diplomacy, wars, invasions, alliances. A slot frees up again when its faction has no colonies left.
factionflag <faction> [option]: changes any faction's flag.
no option: a popup shows the flags as pictures; browse with Next/Previous or the arrow keys
random: a random player flag
a number: that player flag (factionflag list numbers them)
another faction: copies its flag
reset: its own flag again

factionlore <faction> [option]: the text on the faction's page in the Intel screen. Works for every faction.
no option: shows the text
any text: replaces it (a | starts a new paragraph; don't use ;, the console splits commands there)
add <text>: adds a paragraph
reset: brings back the original

These three shape a faction made with spawnfaction. Without an option, each one shows the current setting, and every setting stays in the save.
factionships <faction> <style>: which ships its new fleets use.
lowtech, midline, hightech: only ships of that tech level
pirate: pirate and low tech ships
all: every ship the sector's factions use
like <faction>: copies that faction completely: the same ships, the same weapons and the same way of fighting. For example, like tritachyon makes it fly Tri-Tachyon ships with Tri-Tachyon tactics.

factiondoctrine <faction> <preset>: how its fleets are put together and how they fight. Presets add up (for example aggressive, then carriers, then elite); a new one replaces an earlier one that sets the same thing.
aggressive: its captains charge in and fight to the end
cautious: its captains keep their distance and pull back sooner
carriers: mostly carriers and fighters
phase: mostly phase ships
warships: mostly gun ships, few carriers or phase ships
elite: fewer ships, but the best quality and officers
swarm: many cheap, small ships with weak officers
capitals: mostly big ships
reset: back to the doctrine of the faction it copies

factionpersonality <faction> <type>: how it behaves towards others.
warlike: declares war easily and tires of it slowly
peaceful: never starts wars itself and tires of them quickly
pirate: Nexerelin treats it as a pirate faction: hostile to everyone except pirates, free ports, nothing illegal
lawful: back to normal diplomacy after pirate
expansionist: sends colony expeditions often
isolationist: sends no colony expeditions
normal: undoes all of the above

Faction strength
factionpower <faction> [clear]: colonies, stability, unrest, disrupted industries, garrisons, Nexerelin invasion points and troop reserves, and any Worldsmith effects with how long they last.
clear: ends the Worldsmith effects early

weakenfaction <faction> [1-3]: first shows what will happen in each colony, then asks. It all wears off by itself.
1: unrest for about 6 months
2: also a 6-month growth freeze, weaker garrisons, defenses disrupted for 4 months, fewer invasion points
3: lasts up to 3 years: 3-year growth freeze, stability -3 fading by 1 a year, military and ship industries disrupted for 1-2 years, drained troops and invasion points

strengthenfaction <faction> [1-3]: the same in reverse.
1: clears unrest and disruptions, lifts Worldsmith growth freezes
2: also repairs garrisons, adds troops and invasion points, +2 stability for 6 months
3: also +3 stability fading by 1 a year, and many more invasion points

expeditions [option]: Nexerelin's colony expeditions. Nexerelin sends one every few months and picks the faction by share.
no options: every faction's share and how often expeditions come
<faction> 30%: that faction sends 30% of all expeditions; the others share the rest in their usual proportions. 100% = only that faction.
<faction> off: it sends none
<faction> reset: its usual share again
frequency 200%: expeditions come twice as often (50% = half as often)
reset: everything back to normal

War and peace
wars [faction]: who is at war with whom, the alliances, and how war-weary each faction is. With a faction: its relation (-100 to 100) with every other faction.
totalwar [withplayer]: every faction with colonies goes to war with every other one, and all alliances break up. Asks first.
withplayer: you join in too (with a commission you share your employer's wars anyway)

totalpeace [all] [withplayer]: every faction with colonies makes peace. Asks first.
all: pirates too
withplayer: you too

armada <faction> [system] [small|medium|large]: that faction's war fleet jumps into the system (or the one you are in), attacks its biggest colony for about two months, then leaves. If the two factions aren't at war, only the armada turns hostile; no war is declared.
small / medium / large: its size (medium if you leave it out)

rebellion [colony] [faction]: a Nexerelin rebellion in one colony. The rebels fight for the faction you name, or for one Nexerelin picks, or for independence. If they win, the colony changes hands.

Apocalypse
apocalypse <scenario> [all] asks first. Your own colonies are spared unless you add all.
remnant: an elite Remnant armada attacks every inhabited system for about two months, then leaves.
bombard: every colony is saturation-bombed into ruins; story-critical worlds survive. This can't be undone.
revolution: Nexerelin rebellions break out in every colony of size 3 or more.

Credits: LazyWizard and Lukas04 (Console Commands), LazyWizard (LazyLib), Histidine (Nexerelin). MIT license.

You can modify orbits, terraform planets, rename entities, and create custom factions with specific ships and doctrines. It also allows for large-scale geopolitical changes like total war, peace treaties, armadas, and apocalyptic scenarios.
saveCompatibilityText: Can be added to a running save, but not removed from one.
